api/csharp/Polars.CSharp.AdbcIngestMode..summary: Enum AdbcIngestMode Namespace Polars.CSharp Assembly Polars.CSharp.dll Specifies the behavior when bulk ingesting a DataFrame into an ADBC database table. public enum AdbcIngestMode Fields Append = 1 Appends the data to an existing table. Fails if the target table does not exist, or if the DataFrame schema doesn't match. Create = 0 Creates a new table and inserts the data. Fails if the target table already exists. (Default behavior) Replace = 2 Drops the target table if it already exists, creates a new one, and inserts the data. Extremely useful for overriding temporary/staging tables.

Optimizes the layout of the Delta table by compacting small files (bin-packing) and optionally applying Z-Order clustering. api/csharp/Polars.CSharp.JoinSide.html.summary: Enum JoinSide Namespace Polars.CSharp Assembly Polars.CSharp.dll Specifies the strategy for the hash join build side. In a hash join, one dataframe is loaded into memory (the "build side") to construct a hash table, while the other is streamed (the "probe side") to find matches. Generally, the smaller dataframe should be the build side for optimal performance and memory usage. public enum JoinSide : byte Fields ForceLeft = 2 Force using the left side as the build side. ForceRight = 4 Force using the right side as the build side. LetPolarsDecide = 0 Let Polars decide the best join strategy (Optimizer's choice). PreferLeft = 1 Prefer using the left side as the build side (hash table). Optimizer may override this if the right side is significantly smaller. PreferRight = 3 Prefer using the right side as the build side (hash table). Optimizer may override this if the left side is significantly smaller.

api/csharp/Polars.CSharp.RankMethod.html.summary: Enum RankMethod Namespace Polars.CSharp Assembly Polars.CSharp.dll public enum RankMethod : byte Fields Average = 0 The average of the ranks that would have been assigned to all the tied values is assigned to each value. Dense = 3 Like ‘min’, but the rank of the next highest element is assigned the rank immediately after those assigned to the tied elements. Max = 2 The maximum of the ranks that would have been assigned to all the tied values is assigned to each value. Min = 1 The minimum of the ranks that would have been assigned to all the tied values is assigned to each value. (This is also referred to as “competition” ranking.) Ordinal = 4 All values are given a distinct rank, corresponding to the order that the values occur in the Series. Random = 5 Like ‘ordinal’, but the rank for ties is not dependent on the order that the values occur in the Series.

api/csharp/Polars.CSharp.RoundMode.html.title: Enum RoundMode | Polars.NET
api/csharp/Polars.CSharp.RoundMode.html.summary: Enum RoundMode Namespace Polars.CSharp Assembly Polars.CSharp.dll public enum RoundMode Fields HalfAwayFromZero = 0 Round to the nearest value; break ties by rounding away from zero. For example, 0.5 rounds to 1, -0.5 rounds to -1, 2.5 rounds to 3. Also known as “commercial rounding”. HalfToEven = 1 Round to the nearest value; break ties by choosing the nearest even value. For example, 0.5 rounds to 0, 1.5 rounds to 2, 2.5 rounds to 2. Also known as “banker’s rounding”; this is the default because it tends to minimise cumulative rounding bias. ToZero = 2 Always round (truncate) towards zero, discarding the fractional part beyond decimals. For example, 0.9 rounds to 0, -0.9 rounds to 0, 1.29 rounds to 1.2 (with decimals=1). Equivalent to the truncate() method.

api/csharp/Polars.CSharp.WindowMappingSt.summary: Enum WindowMappingStrategy Namespace Polars.CSharp Assembly Polars.CSharp.dll public enum WindowMappingStrategy : byte Fields Explode = 1 If the aggregation may result in multiple values per group, map each value to a new row, similar to the results of group_by + agg + explode. If the aggregation always results in one scalar value per group, map this value to one row position. Sorting of the given groups is required if the groups are not part of the window operation for the operation, otherwise the result would not make sense. This operation changes the number of rows. GroupsToRows = 0 If the aggregation results in multiple values per group, map them back to their row position in the DataFrame. This can only be done if each group yields the same elements before aggregation as after. If the aggregation results in one scalar value per group, this value will be mapped to every row. Join = 2 If the aggregation may result in multiple values per group, join the values as List{group_dtype} to each row position. Warning: this can be memory intensive. If the aggregation always results in one scalar value per group, join this value as group_dtype to each row position.

api/fsharp/DataFrameDeltaExtensions.html.summary: DataFrameDeltaExtensions Namespace: Polars.FSharp MergeDeltaOrdered Starts a fluent builder to merge a DataFrame into a Delta Lake table with strict, order-preserving SQL MERGE semantics. Unlike traditional merge methods, this builder guarantees that chained actions (Update, Delete, Insert) are evaluated exactly in the order they are defined. If no actions are specified before execution, it intelligently defaults to a standard Upsert (WhenMatchedUpdate + WhenNotMatchedInsert). // Signature: this: DataFrame -> path: string -> mergeKeys: Seq<string> -> canEvolve: Option<bool> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> DeltaMergeBuilder Parameters Name Type Description this DataFrame - path string The URI to the target Delta Lake table (local or cloud). mergeKeys Seq<string> The column names to join on (must exist in both the Source DataFrame and Target Delta table). canEvolve Option<bool> If set to true, allows schema evolution (e.g., adding new columns from the Source to the Target). Default is false. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud storage credentials and configuration (e.g., AWS S3, Azure Blob). Returns A DeltaMergeBuilder instance used to chain match conditions, culminating in a call to .Execute().

api/fsharp/Delta.html.summary: Delta Namespace: Polars.FSharp AddFeature Enables a specific feature on the Delta Table. WARNING: Enabling features may upgrade the Delta Protocol version (e.g., to Reader v3 / Writer v7). Older readers may not be able to read the table after this operation. // Signature: path: string -> featureName: string -> allowProtocolIncrease: Option<bool> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> Void Parameters Name Type Description path string The root URI of the Delta table. featureName string The name of the feature to enable (use DeltaTableFeatures constants). allowProtocolIncrease Option<bool> If true, allows the operation to upgrade the table's Protocol Version if the feature requires it. If false, and the current protocol is too low, the operation will fail. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud storage credentials. Delete Deletes rows from a Delta Lake table that match a given predicate. By default, this operation performs a Copy-on-Write (CoW), meaning any underlying data files containing matching rows are entirely rewritten. Note: If Deletion Vectors are enabled on the table, this operation automatically shifts to a Merge-on-Read (MoR) approach. Instead of expensive file rewrites, deleted rows are swiftly marked in a separate deletion vector file, which drastically improves deletion performance. // Signature: path: string -> predicate: Expr -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> Void Parameters Name Type Description path string Path to the Delta table. predicate Expr Filter expression to identify rows to delete. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud storage configuration. History Returns provenance information, including the operation, user, timestamp, etc., for each write to a table. // Signature: path: string -> limit: Option<int> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> DataFrame Parameters Name Type Description path string The root URI of the Delta table. limit Option<int> The number of latest commits to retrieve. Set to 0 (default) to retrieve all history. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud storage credentials. Returns A DataFrame containing the commit history. Optimize Optimizes the layout of the Delta table by compacting small files (bin-packing) and optionally applying Z-Order clustering. This operation significantly improves read performance by reducing the number of files and co-locating related data. Note: If Deletion Vectors (DV) are enabled on the table, any soft-deleted rows tracked by the vectors will be physically removed (materialized) from the newly compacted Parquet files, effectively clearing the deletion vectors for the optimized partitions. // Signature: path: string -> targetSizeMb: Option<int64> -> partitionFilters: Option<Seq<Tuple<string, string>>> -> zOrderColumns: Option<Seq<string>> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> int64 Parameters Name Type Description path string The root URI of the Delta table. targetSizeMb Option<int64> The target file size in Megabytes for the compacted files (default: 128 MB). partitionFilters Option<Seq<Tuple<string, string>>> Optional sequence of partition key-value pairs to restrict optimization to specific partitions. Example: [ ("date", "2024-01-01") ] zOrderColumns Option<Seq<string>> Optional sequence of column names to apply Z-Order clustering. Z-Ordering co-locates data based on these columns, significantly speeding up queries that filter on them. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud storage credentials and configuration. Returns The number of new data files created during the optimization process. Restore Restores the Delta table to a previous state defined by a specific version or timestamp. Note: This operation creates a new commit (version) that reflects the state of the table at the target point. // Signature: path: string -> version: Option<UInt64> -> timestamp: Option<DateTime> -> ignoreMissingFiles: Option<bool> -> protocolDowngradeAllowed: Option<bool> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> UInt64 Parameters Name Type Description path string The root URI of the Delta table. version Option<UInt64> The specific version number to restore to. Set to null if restoring by timestamp. timestamp Option<DateTime> The timestamp to restore to. Set to null if restoring by version. ignoreMissingFiles Option<bool> If true, the restore operation will ignore missing files (e.g., those deleted by Vacuum). If false, it will fail if any required files are missing. protocolDowngradeAllowed Option<bool> Whether to allow downgrading the Delta Protocol version during restore (rarely needed). cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud storage credentials. Returns The new version number of the table after the restore operation. (Alias for standard Col(), adds semantic clarity) // Signature: columnName: string -> Expr Parameters Name Type Description columnName string - Vacuum Recursively delete files and directories in the table that are no longer needed by the table for maintaining the transaction history. // Signature: path: string -> retentionHours: Option<int> -> enforceRetention: Option<bool> -> dryRun: Option<bool> -> vacuumModeFull: Option<bool> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> int64 Parameters Name Type Description path string The root URI of the Delta table (e.g., "s3://bucket/table"). retentionHours Option<int> The retention threshold in hours. Files removed before this threshold will be deleted. Faster. true (Full): Scans the entire storage directory to find and remove any files not referenced in the transaction log (including orphan files from failed writes). Slower but more thorough. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud storage credentials and configuration (e.g. AWS Keys, Azure Secrets). Returns The number of files deleted (or selected for deletion in dry-run mode).

api/fsharp/LazyFrameDeltaExtensions.html.summary: LazyFrameDeltaExtensions Namespace: Polars.FSharp MergeDeltaOrdered Starts a fluent builder to merge a LazyFrame into a Delta Lake table with strict, order-preserving SQL MERGE semantics. api/fsharp/UnityCatalog.html.summary: UnityCatalog Namespace: Polars.FSharp CreateCatalogTable Creates a new table registration within the Unity Catalog. // Signature: (instance) catalogName: string -> schemaName: string -> tableName: string -> polarsSchema: PolarsSchema -> tableType: Option<CatalogTableType> -> storageLocation: Option<string> -> Void Parameters Name Type Description catalogName string The name of the catalog where the table will be created. schemaName string The name of the schema (database) within the catalog. tableName string The name of the table to be created. polarsSchema PolarsSchema The structural definition of the table columns and data types via PolarsSchema. tableType Option<CatalogTableType> The management type of the table. Managed: Unity Catalog manages both metadata and physical data. External: Unity Catalog manages metadata, but data resides at a specific storageLocation. storageLocation Option<string> The physical URI for the table data (e.g., s3://my-bucket/path/). Required if tableType is set to External; typically null for Managed tables. DeleteCatalogRecords Deletes records from a Unity Catalog table that match the specified predicate. This operation is ACID-compliant and leverages the underlying Delta Lake protocol. If Deletion Vectors (DVs) are enabled on the table, it performs a metadata-only delete; otherwise, it performs a physical rewrite of the affected data files. // Signature: (instance) catalogName: string -> schemaName: string -> tableName: string -> predicate: Expr -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> Void Parameters Name Type Description catalogName string The name of the catalog containing the table. schemaName string The name of the schema (database) containing the table. tableName string The name of the table from which records will be removed. predicate Expr A boolean Expr defining the condition for rows to be deleted. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud-specific configurations including storage credentials and retry policies for concurrent conflicts. DeleteCatalogTable Deletes (drops) a table from the Unity Catalog. For Managed tables, this typically removes both the metadata and the underlying physical data. For External tables, only the metadata registration is removed, leaving the physical data intact in your cloud storage. // Signature: (instance) catalogName: string -> schemaName: string -> tableName: string -> Void Parameters Name Type Description catalogName string The name of the catalog containing the table. schemaName string The name of the schema (database) containing the table. tableName string The name of the table to be deleted. DeltaHistory Retrieves the commit history (audit trail) for a Unity Catalog Delta table as a DataFrame. This includes metadata about who performed what operation, when it occurred, and what parameters were used. // Signature: (instance) catalogName: string -> schemaName: string -> tableName: string -> limit: Option<int> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> DataFrame Parameters Name Type Description catalogName string The name of the catalog (e.g., "main"). schemaName string The name of the schema/database (e.g., "default"). tableName string The name of the table to audit. limit Option<int> The maximum number of history commits to retrieve. If 0, retrieves all available history. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud-specific configurations and credentials resolved via Unity Catalog. Returns A DataFrame containing the flattened and formatted history of the table. Note Data Processing: The raw JSON history from the Delta log is automatically processed: Timestamps are cast to UTC Datetime. Complex fields like operationMetrics and operationParameters are unnested into flat columns. Columns are reordered to place essential information (version, timestamp, operation) at the beginning. Note on Versioning: For standard DML operations, the version column might be null in the raw log; rows are sorted by version or timestamp in descending order (latest first) by default. DeltaRestore Restores a Unity Catalog Delta table to a previous state based on a version number or a timestamp. This operation is atomic and ACID-compliant. // Signature: (instance) catalogName: string -> schemaName: string -> tableName: string -> version: Option<UInt64> -> timestamp: Option<DateTime> -> ignoreMissingFiles: Option<bool> -> protocolDowngradeAllowed: Option<bool> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> UInt64 Parameters Name Type Description catalogName string The name of the catalog (e.g., "main"). schemaName string The name of the schema/database (e.g., "default"). tableName string The name of the table to restore. version Option<UInt64> The specific Delta table version to restore to. Mutually exclusive with timestamp. timestamp Option<DateTime> The specific DateTime to restore the table state to. Mutually exclusive with version. ignoreMissingFiles Option<bool> If true, allows the restore to proceed even if some underlying data files are missing from storage. Use with caution as this may result in a partial restoration. protocolDowngradeAllowed Option<bool> If true, allows the table to be restored to a version that requires a lower protocol reader/writer version than the current one. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud-specific configurations and credentials resolved via Unity Catalog. Returns The new version number of the table after the restore operation is committed. Note How it works: Instead of physically deleting newer data, Restore creates a new commit in the transaction log that reverts the table's metadata and file references to the target state. Safety: This operation will fail if any required data files have been physically removed (e.g., by a Vacuum operation) unless ignoreMissingFiles is set to true. DeltaVacuum Physically deletes data files that are no longer referenced by the Delta table and are older than the specified retention threshold. This operation helps reduce storage costs and ensures compliance by removing historical data that is no longer needed. // Signature: (instance) catalogName: string -> schemaName: string -> tableName: string -> retentionHours: Option<int> -> enforceRetention: Option<bool> -> dryRun: Option<bool> -> vacuumModeFull: Option<bool> -> cloudOptions: Option<CloudOptions> -> int64 Parameters Name Type Description catalogName string The name of the catalog (e.g., "main"). schemaName string The name of the schema/database (e.g., "default"). tableName string The name of the table to vacuum. retentionHours Option<int> The number of hours to retain historical files. Files modified within this window will not be deleted. If null, the table's default retention setting is used. enforceRetention Option<bool> If true, the operation will fail if retentionHours is less than the table's minimum retention (usually 168h). Set to false only for emergency cleanup, at the risk of corrupting active readers. dryRun Option<bool> If true, the method returns the number of files that would be deleted without actually removing them. vacuumModeFull Option<bool> If true, performs a full scan of the object store to find unreferenced files. If false (Lite mode), uses the Delta log to identify files to be removed. cloudOptions Option<CloudOptions> Cloud-specific configurations and credentials resolved via Unity Catalog. Returns The total number of physical files deleted from storage (or identified for deletion if dryRun is true). Note Warning: This is a destructive operation. Once files are vacuumed, you can no longer "Time Travel" to versions that relied on those files. Retention Period: By default, Delta Lake prevents deleting files younger than 168 hours (7 days) to protect active readers and concurrent transactions. articles/intro.html.title: Introduction to Polars.NET | Polars.NET
articles/intro.html.summary: Introduction to Polars.NET Welcome to Polars.NET. This guide provides practical advice and patterns to help you get the most out of the library. Core Concepts Understanding these two modes is crucial for performance: 1. Lazy vs. Eager Eager (DataFrame): Execution happens immediately. Data is loaded into memory. This is similar to List<T> or DataTable. Use this for debugging or small datasets. Lazy (LazyFrame): No execution happens until you call Collect(). Polars builds a "Query Plan", optimizes it (predicate pushdown, projection pushdown), and then executes. Rule of Thumb: Always start with Lazy (LazyFrame). Only convert to Eager (DataFrame) when you need to inspect the final results or materialize data for the UI. 2. Expressions (Expr) In Polars.NET, you don't manipulate data directly in loops. You construct Expr objects that tell the engine what to do. // Avoid: Traditional C# loops (Slow, data copying) foreach(var row in df.Rows()) { ... } // Do: Use Expressions (Fast, SIMD, Parallel) df.Select( Col("A").Sum(), Col("B").Filter(Col("A") > 10).Mean() ); 3.Practical Advice (Best Practices) 1. Prefer Scan over Read When dealing with files (CSV, Parquet, IPC), use the Scan methods provided by LazyFrame. ReadCsv: Loads the entire file into RAM. Prone to Out-Of-Memory (OOM) on large files. ScanCsv: Returns a LazyFrame. It only reads the headers initially. When you filter or select columns later, the reader will only read the necessary bytes from the disk. 2. Handle "Big Data" with Streaming If your dataset is larger than your available RAM, standard execution might fail. Polars.NET supports an out-of-core streaming engine. // This enables the streaming engine to process data in chunks // keeping memory usage low and stable. var result = lazyFrame.Collect(useStreaming:true); 3. Native Expressions > UDFs While Polars.NET supports high-performance C# User Defined Functions (UDFs), they are opaque to the optimizer. Native: Col("A") + Col("B") -> Runs in Rust, uses SIMD, multi-threaded. UDF: Col("A").Map(x => x + 1) -> Calls back into C#, no SIMD, strictly row-wise or chunk-wise. Advice: Only use Map if the logic cannot be expressed using the built-in Expr functions (e.g., calling an external API or a complex .NET library). 4. Memory Management (using) Polars.NET objects (DataFrame, Series, LazyFrame) wrap native Rust memory handles. While we implement Finalizers, relying on GC for large data objects can cause memory pressure. For critical hot paths or huge datasets, use the using statement to deterministic release native memory: using var df = DataFrame.ReadCsv("data.csv"); using var filtered = df.Filter(Col("id") > 100); // Native memory is freed immediately here 5. C# vs F# Polars.NET offers two distinct APIs tailored for each language's strengths: C#: Uses a fluent, method-chaining style similar to LINQ. Best for: Production engineering, web services, building typed wrappers. F#: Uses a functional, pipeline-operator (|>) style. Best for: Data exploration, scripting, notebooks, and complex transformations. 6. Performance Pitfalls Iterating Rows: Avoid converting a DataFrame to IEnumerable or iterating rows manually unless absolutely necessary. This breaks the zero-copy advantage and incurs heavy marshalling costs. Premature Collection: Don't call .Collect() in the middle of a transformation chain. Keep the chain lazy as long as possible to let the optimizer do its job. Strings are expensive: Operations on String columns are generally slower than numeric types. If you have categorical data (e.g., "US", "CN", "JP"), cast them to Categorical type for faster grouping and sorting. // Cast string column to Categorical for performance df.WithColumns(Col("Country").Cast(DataType.Categorical)); 7. Getting Help API Reference: Link to API Docs Polars Rust Documentation: Since this is a wrapper with C ABI layer, the core logic is relatively same to the main Polars project. Concepts from the official Polars guide often apply here.

articles/quickstart.html.title: Getting Started | Polars.NET
articles/quickstart.html.summary: Getting Started This guide will walk you through the core functionalities of Polars.NET: creating DataFrames, inspecting data, applying transformations, and leveraging the Lazy engine for maximum performance. Prerequisites First, install the NuGet packages. dotnet add package Polars.NET # For F# users (includes idiomatic extensions) dotnet add package Polars.FSharp 1. Creating a DataFrame Polars.NET supports creating DataFrames from CSV, Parquet, JSON, Database, or in-memory objects. C# (Fluent API) using Polars; using Polars.CSharp; using static Polars.CSharp.Polars; // Allows using Col(), Lit() directly // Create from in-memory columns var df = DataFrame.FromColumns(new { Date = new[] { "2023-01-01", "2023-01-01", "2023-01-02" }, City = new[] { "London", "Manchester", "London" }, Temperature = new[] { 10.5, 9.0, 12.1 }, Rain = new[] { true, true, false } }); // Parse date string to Date32 type df = df.WithColumn(Col("Date").Str.ToDate("%Y-%m-%d")); // Preview df.Show(); F# (Pipeline API) open Polars.FSharp type WeatherData = { Date: string; City: string; Temperature: float; Rain: bool } let data = [ { Date="2023-01-01"; City="London"; Temperature=10.5; Rain=true } { Date="2023-01-01"; City="Manchester"; Temperature=9.0; Rain=true } { Date="2023-01-02"; City="London"; Temperature=12.1; Rain=false } ] let df = DataFrame.ofRecords data |> pl.withColumn (pl.col("Date").Str.ToDate "%Y-%m-%d") // In F#, the DataFrame prints nicely in interactive sessions df 2. Selection & Filtering Polars expressions allow you to define transformations efficiently. Notice how C# uses method chaining, while F# uses the pipe operator (|>). C# var londonData = df .Filter(Col("City") == "London") .Select( Col("Date"), // Arithmetic on columns (Col("Temperature") * 1.8 + 32).Alias("Temp_F") ); F# let londonData = df |> pl.filter (pl.col "City" .== pl.lit "London") |> pl.select [ pl.col "Date" // Arithmetic using overloaded operators (pl.col "Temperature" * pl.lit 1.8 + pl.lit 32.0).Alias "Temp_F" ] 3. Aggregation (GroupBy) Compute summary statistics by groups. Polars executes aggregations in parallel. C# var aggDf = df .GroupBy("City") .Agg( Col("Temperature").Mean().Alias("Avg_Temp"), Col("Temperature").Max().Alias("Max_Temp"), Col("Rain").Sum().Alias("Rainy_Days"), // Sum of bool = count true Col("City").Count().Alias("Total_Records") ); F# let aggDf = df |> pl.groupBy [pl.col "City"] [ pl.col("Temperature").Mean().Alias "Avg_Temp" pl.col("Temperature").Max().Alias "Max_Temp" pl.col("Rain").Sum().Alias "Rainy_Days" pl.count().Alias "Total_Records" ] 4. Window Functions Window functions allow you to compute values relative to a group without collapsing the rows (unlike GroupBy). This is extremely powerful for time-series analysis or calculating differences from averages. C# // Calculate daily average and the difference from that average var windowDf = df.Select( Col("Date"), Col("City"), Col("Temperature"), // Window Expression: Mean over Date Col("Temperature").Mean().Over("Date").Alias("Daily_Avg"), // Calculate difference immediately (Col("Temperature") - Col("Temperature").Mean().Over("Date")).Alias("Diff") ).Sort("Date", descending: false); F# let windowDf = df |> pl.select [ pl.col "Date" pl.col "City" pl.col "Temperature" (pl.col("Temperature").Mean().Over(pl.col "Date")).Alias "Daily_Avg" (pl.col "Temperature" - pl.col("Temperature").Mean().Over(pl.col "Date")).Alias "Diff" ] |> pl.sort (pl.col "Date", false) 5. The Lazy API (Performance) This is where Polars.NET shines. Instead of executing every step immediately, Lazy() builds a query plan. Collect() optimizes and runs it. Why Lazy? Predicate Pushdown: Filters are applied before loading data (if possible). Projection Pushdown: Only necessary columns are loaded. Parallel Execution: Branching logic is executed in parallel. C# var lf = df.Lazy() .Filter(Col("Temperature") > 10.0) .GroupBy("City") .Agg(Col("Temperature").Mean().Alias("Lazy_Avg_Temp")); // See the optimized query plan Console.WriteLine(lf.Explain()); // Execute var finalDf = lf.Collect(); F# let lf = df.Lazy() |> LazyFrame.filter (pl.col "Temperature" .> pl.lit 10.0) |> LazyFrame.groupBy [pl.col "City"] [ pl.mean(pl.col "Temperature").Alias "Lazy_Avg_Temp" ] printfn "%s" (lf.Explain(optimized=true)) let finalDf = lf.Collect() Next Steps IO Operations: Learn how to read/write CSV, Parquet, and Excel. User Defined Functions: Learn how to map C# functions for custom logic. API Reference: Explore the full list of available Expressions.

index.html.summary: Polars.NET Polars.NET brings the Polars data processing engine to the .NET ecosystem. 1. QuickStart using Polars.CSharp; using static Polars.CSharp.Polars; // For Col(), Lit() helpers // 1. Create a DataFrame var data = new[] { new { Name = "Alice", Age = 25, Dept = "IT" }, new { Name = "Bob", Age = 30, Dept = "HR" }, new { Name = "Charlie", Age = 35, Dept = "IT" } }; var df = DataFrame.From(data); // 2. Filter & Aggregate var res = df. Lazy() .Filter(Col("Age") > 28) .GroupBy("Dept") .Agg( Col("Age").Mean().Alias("AvgAge"), Col("Name").Count().Alias("Count") ) .Sort("AvgAge"); // 3.
